82/51->87/53 (bands=hypotensive/hypotensive); RR 10->9 (band=bradypneic)

A 31-year-old female presents to the emergency department following an assault involving multiple
kicks to her torso. She is conscious and denies head trauma. Her medical history includes
endometriosis and previous surgical removal of a tubo-ovarian abscess. She takes oral contraceptives.
Her vital signs show: temperature 97.3°F (36.9°C), blood pressure 87/53 mmHg, pulse 149/min,
respiratory rate 9/min, and oxygen saturation 94% on room air. Physical examination reveals facial
lacerations, severe chest and abdominal bruising, clear lung sounds, and a soft but distended
abdomen with diffuse tenderness. Her skin is cool and clammy. A FAST exam shows fluid in the
peri-splenic space. What is the most appropriate immediate step in management? Answer Choices: (A)
Emergency laparotomy (B) Administration of vasopressors (C) Thoracentesis (D) Blood transfusion (E)
Fluid resuscitation (F) CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis (G) Observation and serial abdominal
exams (H) Diagnostic peritoneal lavage (I) Needle decompression (J) Peritoneal drainage
 A. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis
B. Administration of vasopressors
C. Observation and serial abdominal exams
D. Thoracentesis
E. Peritoneal drainage
F. Needle decompression
G. Diagnostic peritoneal lavage
H. Emergency laparotomy
I. Fluid resuscitation
J. Blood transfusion
